strings.settings.page.name: Settings
strings.settings.appearance.glass.title: Glass style
strings.settings.appearance.glass.desc.macos: The material behind the window. Liquid Glass needs macOS 26 or later. Off uses a solid dark background, which is what Linux always gets.
strings.settings.appearance.glass.desc.windows: The material behind the window. Default uses Windows acrylic. Mica and Mica Alt are the quieter Windows 11 materials. Off uses a solid dark background, which is what Linux always gets.
strings.settings.appearance.glass.desc.linux: Linux has no window glass, so the background is always solid dark.
strings.settings.appearance.menuBlur.title: Menu blur
strings.settings.appearance.menuBlur.desc: How strongly context menus blur the content behind them.
strings.settings.appearance.motion.title: Motion level
strings.settings.appearance.motion.desc: Controls UI motion. Reduced uses fades only; None disables animation.
strings.settings.terminal.appearance.font.title: Font
strings.settings.terminal.appearance.font.desc: Typeface used to render terminal text.
ANSI color palette for terminal text. Background stays fixed.
strings.settings.terminal.appearance.runningOutl: Animate the outline while a command runs
Animates the terminal card's outline while a command is executing, so you can see at a glance that the terminal is busy. Requires shell integration (zsh, bash and PowerShell).
Which animation the outline runs. The app-wide motion setting overrides this: Reduced forces Breath, and None keeps the outline static.

Full-screen apps like vim, less and top — and inline interactive apps like Claude Code, a REPL, or an ssh session — keep the shell's command marker set for their whole session, so the outline would animate the entire time. Off by default: the outline stays static while they are in the foreground. Apps that report progress (OSC 9;4) still animate it either way.
strings.settings.terminal.session.scrollback.des: Number of lines kept in the terminal scrollback buffer.
strings.settings.terminal.session.defaultCwd.des: Directory used when opening a new terminal tab. Leave blank to use your home directory.
strings.settings.terminal.session.shell.title: Shell
strings.settings.terminal.session.shell.desc: Executable used for new terminals. Leave empty to auto-detect.
strings.settings.terminal.session.shellArgs.desc: Arguments passed to the shell. Quotes are supported.
strings.settings.terminal.session.iterm2Compat.d: Luneterm normally identifies itself honestly (TERM_PROGRAM=Luneterm). Turn this on to report iTerm2 instead, which unlocks features some apps enable only for iTerm2 — but also invites apps to assume iTerm2 protocols Luneterm does not implement, such as inline images. Applies to new terminal tabs; open tabs keep the identity they started with.
Confirm before closing a running tab
Show a confirmation dialog before closing a terminal tab with a running session.
Allow apps to write to the clipboard
Lets command-line programs in the terminal copy text to your system clipboard (OSC 52). Turn off to block clipboard writes from terminal apps.
When on, Option+key sends Meta (Esc-prefixed) sequences, e.g. Option+B/F to move by word and Option+Delete to delete a word, instead of typing special characters. Has no effect on Windows and Linux, where Alt always acts as Meta.
strings.settings.about.name: Luneterm
strings.settings.about.blurb: A standalone terminal for macOS, Windows and Linux. Its engine is a Rust port of xterm.js 6.0.0.
strings.settings.about.notice.avalonia: Avalonia acrylic noise and colour formulas
strings.luneui.settings-page.restart-message: Shell changes apply to new terminal tabs.
strings.menu.app.name: Luneterm menu
strings.menu.terminal.name: Terminal menu
strings.settings.terminal.session.shellIntegrati: Starts new zsh, bash and PowerShell sessions through small scripts Luneterm writes to its own folder. They report the working directory and when a command starts and ends, which tabs and the running outline use. Your own startup files run as usual. Turn off to start the shell exactly as the terminal would without them. Applies to new terminal tabs.
